class_name: 進行-慣習-コトニナッテイル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: ことになる (an outcome that comes about) in the ている form: a standing arrangement, schedule or regulation that holds independently of the speaker's will, which is why it is the standard way to explain workplace and school rules. Compare ことにしている, which reports the speaker's own resolve; Japanese often prefers ことになっている even for decisions the speaker did make, to keep the statement impersonal. ことになってる is the everyday spoken form.

examples.ruby: 面接[めんせつ]の結果[けっか]は来週[らいしゅう]伝[つた]えることになっている。
examples.english: The interview results are due to be given out next week.

examples.ruby: この部屋[へや]では靴[くつ]を脱[ぬ]ぐことになってる。
examples.english: You're supposed to take your shoes off in this room.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]が資料[しりょう]を用意[ようい]することになっています。
examples.english: It's been arranged for the new hire to prepare the materials.
